item.p: The editor explains his supplement ἐν Τεβτ(ύνι) (?) as follows: "I presume that this line, like 1.8, projected about five letters farther to the left than the following lines. Otherwise there would not be space for the name of the town in which the contract was drawn up, and that information is expected from about 273 B.C. on" (Shelton 1979, p. 220, l. 1 note). The supplement is unnecessary, however, because the location is regularly omitted in the inner script of first-century BCE double documents. The last example of its occurrence is P.Tebt. I 106.1 (101 BCE). Cf., e.g., the roughly-contemporaneous BGU XIV 2389 (Herakleopolite, 72 BCE), whose inner script has only the date before the main verb of the contract. Sometimes even the date is missing: e.g., P.Ryl. IV 587.1 (Tebtunis, 87 BCE) and P.Mert. I 6.1 (Nestou Epoikion, 77 BCE). For a list of late-Ptolemaic double documents, see Yiftach-Firanko 2008, p. 210, n. 24, to which the present contract should be added under the category "extensive account of the contract."
